$comment: The catalog's texts in English (components.json has them in Japanese): the same ids. Studio shows these to a page in English (Catalog.InEnglish). Every title, note and description of components.json has its English here (CatalogTests).

noneOption.title: Do nothing
noneOption.description: What .NET 10 lacks fails where it is used. The conversion report lists it.
noneOption.detail: What .NET does not have is stubbed to compile (it throws when run); what it has stays as it is (its exceptions and differences too). Listed in the conversion report

compat.title: Work as before
compat.description: What follows the early end runs as on the original server.
compat.detail: Thread.ResetAbort is replaced with Platform.ResetAbort: the code after the catch runs as on .NET Framework

none.title: Do nothing
none.description: Pages using it can fail with an error.
none.detail: ResetAbort throws (a 503 in the catch after a redirect, for one)

compat.title: Replace it
compat.description: Replaced automatically with what works on .NET 10.
compat.detail: BeginInvoke / EndInvoke are replaced with FrameworkOnCore.AsyncDelegate

none.title: Do nothing
none.description: It fails where it is used.

compat-package.title: Make it work
compat-package.description: Saved data can be read. Reading data from outside is as unsafe as before.
compat-package.detail: System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters and EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization. Existing data can be read. Reading untrusted data is dangerous (as on .NET Framework)

framework.title: As before (Shift_JIS and the like)
framework.description: The encoding of the server's language settings is used.
framework.detail: Encoding.Default is replaced with Platform.DefaultEncoding (Windows: the OS's setting; Linux: LANG's culture)

none.title: As .NET 10 (UTF-8)
none.description: Files and the like can be written in a different encoding, which can garble text.
none.detail: The bytes of files and hashes may differ from .NET Framework's

framework.title: As before
framework.description: Numbers on pages and in reports look as on the original server.
framework.detail: Doubles and floats made text (ToString, concatenation, interpolation, string.Format, Convert.ToString, Append and Write) go through FrameworkNumbers; Parse, TryParse and TimeSpan.From* through FrameworkParsing. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web writes bound values the same way

none.title: As .NET 10
none.description: The number of digits and the rounding can differ from before.
none.detail: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, -0 is "-0", 2.675 as N2 is 2.67; parsing a number too large gives infinity

translations.title: FrameworkOnCore's translations
translations.description: Built-in texts are shown in the languages chosen. The wording can differ slightly from the original server's.
translations.detail: The texts of System.Web and the other ports (Calendar's titles, Login's labels, Wizard's and GridView's buttons, error pages, the exceptions and messages of ASP.NET AJAX, Chart, ASMX, SqlClient and more) in FrameworkOnCore's own translations (the repository's translations/, MIT), in the languages chosen in the application's setting 'Language packs' (by default the ones the original server had language packs for). The wording may differ from Microsoft's

framework.title: Microsoft's translations (Windows servers only)
framework.description: The wording is the original server's. Their license does not allow them on Linux servers.
framework.detail: Satellites made from this machine's .NET Framework language packs (the original server's wording). Microsoft's license forbids distributing them to run on another platform than Windows: only when not deployed on Linux (--deploy none). Microsoft's license terms apply to the deployment

register.title: Make them available (always)
register.description: Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and others can be used.
register.detail: FrameworkOnCore's System.Web (UseWebForms) registers CodePagesEncodingProvider at start: Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and the others are there

stderr.title: Server log on Linux
stderr.description: Windows: the event log. Linux: the server's log (the service's or the container's).
stderr.detail: The event log on Windows; on Linux, the service's journal or the container's log (FrameworkOnCore.EventLogs)

none.title: Do nothing
none.description: On Linux, writing an entry fails.

compat.title: No account on Linux
compat.description: Windows: as before. Linux: works as if there were no account.
compat.detail: WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent and the others are replaced with Platform's

ef6.title: Move to EF6
ef6.description: The code is rewritten automatically to run on the new version.
ef6.detail: Adds Entity Framework 6's package, rewrites the namespaces, embeds the EDMX

compat.title: On Windows only
compat.description: It works on Windows and fails on Linux.
compat.detail: Directory/File.GetAccessControl and the others go to FrameworkOnCore.DirectoryAcl and FileAcl (they throw on Linux)

none.title: Do nothing
none.description: It fails where it is used.

port.title: A version that runs on Linux too
port.description: Works on Windows and Linux (the only option).
port.detail: FrameworkOnCore's System.Drawing.Common (package FrameworkOnCore.Drawing.Common, from dotnet/runtime 6.0's source: GDI+ on Windows, libgdiplus on Linux; the deployment installs libgdiplus and fonts). FrameworkOnCore's System.Web depends on it: every application has it

port.title: Make it work
port.detail: System.Data.Linq ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Data.Linq

none.title: Do nothing
none.detail: Stubbed. DLLs that reference it (System.Web.Mvc's model binding) throw too

retarget.title: Fix the DLLs
retarget.description: The DLLs are rewritten to work on .NET 10 (the originals are kept).
retarget.detail: The types a DLL without source references as "assembly + type" that .NET 10 has in another assembly (CallContext in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web): the converter retargets the DLL's references to them. Members the type lacks are replaced with calls of the compatibility assembly's extension members. The DLL works as it is (the rewritten DLLs are in the output's foc-retargeted)

none.title: Do nothing
none.description: The DLLs fail where they use what has moved.
none.detail: The DLL stays as it is: where it uses those types or members, it throws TypeLoadException or MissingMethodException at run time

port.title: FrameworkOnCore's version
port.description: The original connection settings (database files in App_Data and the like) work as they are.
port.detail: FrameworkOnCore's System.Data.SqlClient (package FrameworkOnCore.Data.SqlClient, from dotnet/maintenance-packages 4.9.0's source). It expands |DataDirectory| in connection strings to App_Data as .NET Framework does, and takes Asynchronous Processing, Network Library and Connection Reset, which .NET rejects (SqlConnectionStringBuilder has the properties of those names too). The web project always has it: Entity Framework's connections and the DLLs' are its

dotnet.title: Microsoft's version
dotnet.description: Some connection settings (App_Data built in code and the like) fail.
dotnet.detail: Microsoft's System.Data.SqlClient package (4.9.0). A connection string built in code with |DataDirectory| throws (the runtime expands the configuration's). Connection strings with Asynchronous Processing, Network Library or Connection Reset throw too

port.title: Make it work
port.description: Pages with charts work as they are.
port.detail: System.Web.DataVisualization ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.DataVisualization (drawn with the ported System.Drawing: it works on Linux too)

port.title: Make it work
port.description: Mobile pages work as they are.
port.detail: System.Web.Mobile ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.Mobile (MobilePage, the mobile: controls, the device adapters)

none.title: Do nothing
none.detail: Stubbed (mobile pages throw). A using alone is removed

corewcf.title: Run them (CoreWCF)
corewcf.description: The web services keep working. Some transports (net.tcp and others) are not supported.
corewcf.detail: The site's .svc services and web.config's system.serviceModel run on CoreWCF within the application (package FrameworkOnCore.ServiceModel): basicHttpBinding, basicHttpsBinding, wsHttpBinding, webHttpBinding (REST), WCF 4's default endpoints and behaviors, serviceActivations, WSDL. The service-side types (ServiceBehavior, WebGet) are rewritten to CoreWCF's. ASP.NET AJAX's enableWebScript too (ScriptManager's ServiceReference, Service.svc/js). Not netTcpBinding, custom ServiceHostFactory, aspNetCompatibilityEnabled (HttpContext.Current in an operation)

none.title: Do nothing
none.description: The web services do not work.
none.detail: The services do not run (.svc answers 404). The service-side types are stubbed

server.title: As the original server
server.description: Built-in texts (calendars, login forms, error pages) are shown in the original server's languages (Japanese and the like). Choose English only for English always.
server.detail: English and the languages the original server had .NET Framework language packs for (capture-culture.ps1 records them; else this machine's). When the UI culture is one chosen, Calendar's, Login's, Wizard's and GridView's texts and error pages are in it. English alone: English whatever the UI culture.

file-name-case.title: File names' upper and lower case

insensitive.title: Not distinguished (as Windows)
insensitive.description: On Linux too, file names are matched regardless of case, as on Windows.
insensitive.detail: The deployment has casefs (libfoccase.so), which start.sh loads

sensitive.title: Distinguished (Linux's way)
sensitive.description: A file named with a different case in the code is not found.
sensitive.detail: A file the application names in another case is not found

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Written in IIS's format and file names: your log tools keep working.
iis.detail: Written as IIS writes it: its format, fields and file names (u_exYYMMDD.log). When writing falls behind, requests wait (no line is dropped). The original server's logFile settings apply

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's
aspnetcore.description: Its format differs slightly from IIS's. Under heavy traffic, some lines can be lost.
aspnetcore.detail: ASP.NET Core's W3CLogger. Its format differs a little from IIS's (no sc-substatus), and it writes up to a limit. It stays as it is once the application is rewritten for ASP.NET Core

off.title: Off
off.description: When the load balancer's log or the like is used instead.
off.detail: No request log (a load balancer's in front, say)

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: web.config's rewrite rules work as on IIS.
iis.detail: The rules run as IIS's URL Rewrite module runs them (inheritance, server variables, Wildcard, the query string's order, redirects' absolute URLs). The original server's globalRules too

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's
aspnetcore.description: Some rules work differently from IIS, and a rule it cannot read stops the application from starting.
aspnetcore.detail: ASP.NET Core's rewriting (AddIISUrlRewrite): the root web.config only, some differences from IIS, and the application does not start with rules it cannot read (subStatusCode, Wildcard, some server variables)

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Error pages are shown as web.config sets them, as on IIS.
iis.detail: Error answers are replaced as IIS replaces them (errorMode, existingResponse, File, ExecuteURL, Redirect). IIS's own pages are simple ones

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's
aspnetcore.description: A short error text only; the error pages you set are not shown.
aspnetcore.detail: A short text for an error without a body. The application's answers are not replaced

off.title: Off
off.detail: An error without a body stays empty

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Responses are compressed as the original server's settings say.
iis.detail: Compressed as the original server's static and dynamic compression are set (without its settings, Windows' defaults: a static file gzipped from its second request within 10 seconds)

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's
aspnetcore.description: Matching responses are compressed every time (not over HTTPS by default).
aspnetcore.detail: Every answer of the types compressed (brotli first; not over HTTPS by default)

off.title: Off
off.description: When the load balancer or a CDN compresses.
off.detail: Left to a load balancer or CDN in front

thread-abort.title: Ending a page early (Response.End and the like)
thread-abort.note: Code that stops a page midway. With the recommended choice, it works as on the original server.
thread-abort.detail: Converter: ResetAbort is replaced with Platform.ResetAbort (it undoes the abort of Response.End in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web). Abort is not supported

async-delegates.title: An old way to run work in the background (BeginInvoke)
async-delegates.note: .NET 10 cannot run it. With the recommended choice, it is replaced automatically with what works.
async-delegates.detail: Converter: replaced with FrameworkOnCore.AsyncDelegate (run on the thread pool)

binary-formatter.title: A data storage format (BinaryFormatter)
binary-formatter.note: An old way to save and restore data as it is. .NET 10 has it off. With the recommended choice, it works, and saved data can be read.
binary-formatter.detail: Converter: the compatibility package System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters and EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization (reading untrusted data is dangerous)

encoding-default.title: The default character encoding (Shift_JIS and the like)
encoding-default.note: The encoding files are read and written in by default. The original server (a Japanese Windows) used Shift_JIS, .NET 10 uses UTF-8. With the recommended choice, it stays as on the original server.
encoding-default.detail: .NET Framework's is the ANSI code page (Shift_JIS on a Japanese Windows), .NET's is UTF-8. Converter: replaced with Platform.DefaultEncoding

floating-point.title: Decimal numbers shown and read
floating-point.note: Where numbers with decimals become text, or are read from text. .NET 10 can show them differently (0.1 + 0.2 as 0.30000000000000004). With the recommended choice, they show as before.
floating-point.detail: Since .NET Core 3.0 a double without a format is the shortest text that round-trips (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004; .NET Framework: 15 digits, 0.3), negative zero is "-0", a fixed precision rounds the exact binary value to even (2.675 as N2 is 2.67; .NET Framework: 2.68, from its 15 digits). Parsing a number too large gives infinity (.NET Framework: an exception). TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.00015) and the others are not rounded to milliseconds. Converter: replaced with FrameworkNumbers and FrameworkParsing (FOC1008, platformReplacements)

language-packs.title: The language of ASP.NET's built-in texts
language-packs.note: The language of built-in texts: calendars, login forms, error pages. On a Japanese Windows server they were in Japanese. With the recommended choice, translations are used.
language-packs.detail: On a server with a language pack (ja on a Japanese Windows, usually) System.Web's texts are in its language when the UI culture is (Calendar's titles, Login's labels, Wizard's buttons, GridView's commands, error pages). .NET has no language packs. Converter: FrameworkOnCore's own translations (translations/) in the languages of the application's setting 'Language packs' (by default the original server's; Microsoft's packs only when chosen and deployed on Windows only: their license forbids distributing them to run elsewhere). CultureInfo.DisplayName (.NET: in the language of Windows' UI): in a translated language that language's, else the original server's English name (FrameworkCultures)

code-pages.title: Character encodings such as Shift_JIS and EUC-JP
code-pages.note: Makes Shift_JIS and the like available on .NET 10. It is always on: nothing to choose.
code-pages.detail: Without a registered provider .NET has only Unicode, ASCII and Latin-1. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web (UseWebForms) registers it at start

system-drawing.title: Creating and editing images (System.Drawing)
system-drawing.note: Draws images and charts. .NET 10 has it on Windows only; it is replaced with a version that runs on Linux too. Text and lines can look slightly different.
system-drawing.detail: .NET's System.Drawing.Common is Windows-only since .NET 7. Converter: FrameworkOnCore's System.Drawing.Common (a port with dotnet/runtime 6.0's Linux implementation, libgdiplus). What it draws (antialiasing, text) differs a little between Windows and Linux. Windows' fonts are not on Linux (Arial and others are replaced with compatible fonts)

charts.title: Charts (the Chart control)
charts.note: Draws charts on pages. .NET 10 does not have it; a version that runs on Linux too is provided.
charts.detail: Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.DataVisualization (the Chart control, ChartImg.axd). Drawn with the ported System.Drawing (libgdiplus on Linux). When ChartImg.axd's image folder (appSettings ChartImageHandler's dir) is on C:, the deployment's setting (APPSETTING_ChartImageHandler) changes it on Linux. Windows Forms' System.Windows.Forms.DataVisualization is not ported

sql-client.title: Connecting to SQL Server
sql-client.note: Connects to the database (SQL Server). .NET 10 rejects some ways of writing the connection settings; with the default, they work as before.
sql-client.detail: .NET's System.Data.SqlClient rejects |DataDirectory| in connection strings (.NET Framework expanded it to App_Data). Converter: the port (FrameworkOnCore.Data.SqlClient) expands it as .NET Framework does

linq-to-sql.title: Database access (LINQ to SQL)
linq-to-sql.note: An old way to read and write the database. .NET 10 does not have it; a version is provided.
linq-to-sql.detail: Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Data.Linq (for SQL Server)

entity-framework-4.title: Database access (Entity Framework 4)
entity-framework-4.note: An old version of a database framework. With the recommended choice, the application is moved to EF6, which runs on .NET 10.
entity-framework-4.detail: Converter: moved to EF6 (its package), the namespaces rewritten

wcf-data-services.title: Data services (WCF Data Services)
wcf-data-services.note: Publishes and reads data over the web. .NET 10 does not have it and the conversion does not cover it: where it is used, it has to be rebuilt.

mobile-controls.title: Pages for mobile phones (mobile controls)
mobile-controls.note: Old page parts for mobile phones. .NET 10 does not have them; a version is provided.
mobile-controls.detail: Deprecated in ASP.NET 4.0 (.NET Framework 4.8 has them). Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.Mobile

wcf-server.title: Providing web services (WCF, .svc)
wcf-server.note: Web services other systems call. .NET 10 cannot run them; they run on a compatible framework (CoreWCF). Some settings are not supported (the conversion report lists them).
wcf-server.detail: .NET's WCF is the client only. Converter: run on CoreWCF (FrameworkOnCore.ServiceModel registers the .svc and web.config's services with CoreWCF)

wcf-client.title: Calling web services (WCF)
wcf-client.note: Calls other systems' web services. The usual ways of calling work on .NET 10.
wcf-client.detail: Converter: the System.ServiceModel.* packages (part of the client only)

event-log.title: Writing to the event log
event-log.note: Writes to Windows' event log. Linux has none; with the default, the entries go to the server's log.

windows-identity.title: Using Windows accounts
windows-identity.note: Finds or switches the Windows account the work runs as. Linux has no Windows accounts.
windows-identity.detail: Converter: Platform's replacements outside Windows (no account)

file-access-control.title: File permissions
file-access-control.note: Reads and sets files' and folders' Windows permissions. Linux cannot.
file-access-control.detail: Windows only. Converter: Directory/File.GetAccessControl and the others go to FrameworkOnCore.DirectoryAcl and FileAcl (they throw outside Windows)

registry.title: The registry
registry.note: Uses Windows' registry. Linux has none: its values cannot be read.
registry.detail: Outside Windows, Registry.LocalMachine and the others are null

oledb.title: Reading Excel and Access files (OLE DB)
oledb.note: Reads Excel and Access files. Windows only: on Linux it has to be rebuilt.
oledb.detail: Windows only: Linux has no provider

directory-services.title: Using Active Directory
directory-services.note: Looks users up in Active Directory. Windows only: on Linux it has to be rebuilt.
directory-services.detail: Windows only. Needs a rewrite to LDAP (System.DirectoryServices.Protocols)

windows-management.title: Windows management (WMI, performance counters, services)
windows-management.note: Reads Windows' state or controls Windows services. Windows only.

code-access-security.title: Old security settings (code access security)
code-access-security.note: An old way to limit a program's permissions. .NET 10 ignores it; for web applications this usually changes nothing.
code-access-security.detail: .NET does nothing with it (there is no partial trust). Web applications usually run in full trust

app-domains.title: Compartments in an application (AppDomain)
app-domains.note: Creates separate compartments inside an application. .NET 10 cannot: where it is used, it has to be rebuilt.

remoting.title: Communication between programs (remoting)
remoting.note: An old way to talk to other programs. .NET 10 does not have it; only commonly used parts are provided.
remoting.detail: Not in .NET. Some of it (CallContext) is in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web and the compatibility assembly

code-dom-compile.title: Compiling code while running (CodeDom)
code-dom-compile.note: Compiles code while the application runs. .NET 10 cannot.
code-dom-compile.detail: .NET's CodeDom does not compile (it throws); it generates code only

web-request.title: Calling the web (WebRequest, WebClient)
web-request.note: An old way to call other web sites. It works on .NET 10 (a rewrite is recommended in the long run).
web-request.detail: Obsolete in .NET but works (HttpClient is recommended)

legacy-crypto.title: Old cryptography
legacy-crypto.note: Old ways to encrypt. They work on .NET 10 (a few settings fail).
legacy-crypto.detail: Obsolete in .NET but works (Rijndael's BlockSize 256 throws)

designers.title: Parts for development tools (designers)
designers.note: Used by Visual Studio's designers. Not needed to run: the conversion removes them.
designers.detail: For Visual Studio's designers. Converter: stubbed, removed from web.config

web-forms.title: ASP.NET pages and services (Web Forms, ASMX and others)
web-forms.note: The application's pages and services themselves. FrameworkOnCore has a version that runs on .NET 10.
web-forms.detail: FrameworkOnCore (System.Web and the others, from WebFormsForCore) has them for .NET

configuration.title: Configuration files (web.config)
configuration.note: Reads web.config and other settings. FrameworkOnCore has a version that runs on .NET 10.

visual-basic-runtime.title: Visual Basic's functions
visual-basic-runtime.note: Built-in functions Visual Basic applications use. .NET 10 has them (a few are provided by a compatibility part).
visual-basic-runtime.detail: .NET's Microsoft.VisualBasic.Core. Some of My's types are in the compatibility assembly

dll-references.title: DLLs without source
dll-references.note: Parts you have as DLLs only. On .NET 10, some of what they use has moved; with the default, the conversion fixes the DLLs.
dll-references.detail: A DLL without source references a type as "assembly + type"; these are types .NET 10 has in another assembly (which ones: APIs; each API is counted in its own component too)
